methods_form.answer: agharsallah

Panel-first, then genome-wide, then a designed submission. (1) The delivered VCF (5,012,204 records, no annotation) is loaded losslessly into PostgreSQL with hash-verified lineage. (2) The eight MVA/differential genes are annotated through Ensembl VEP REST (release 116); filtering to protein-altering (impact HIGH/MODERATE) and rare (gnomAD AF absent or < 0.01) leaves exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous PASS. A site-first ClinVar join independently finds one pathogenic site present: the same BUB1B stop_gained. (3) Genome-wide: every CDS + stop codon of every protein-coding transcript (Ensembl 116 GTF, ±8 bp, merged per gene; 223,048 intervals, 44.6 Mb) is range-joined to the callset → 38,087 distinct coding alleles, all VEP-annotated (191 requests, checkpointed) → 875 rare protein-altering → 65 genes biallelic on PASS calls → exactly 1 with a ClinVar-pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank: BUB1B. (4) A panel-blind phenotype ranker (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python over HPO release 2026-06-23, reading no DNA) ranks BUB1B 6/5,267 on the child's seven own terms; joined to the 65 biallelic genes it is first by a wide margin. (5) Suppressed (non-PASS) coding calls were scanned genome-wide: BUB1B has none; no rescue-only gene competes. (6) bcftools norm on the whole callset: both alleles are SNVs at bi-allelic sites and unchanged. (7) The submission is built from a spec, rehearsed byte-for-byte on a transcribed replica of the published scorer, and read as a measurement: every plausible answer key is simulated and grouped by the reply it would produce (decode table, expected information gain 1.46 bits). Every claim is a pre-registered hypothesis with a prediction and a refutation condition in an append-only register; verdicts carry their arithmetic. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-1/).

Automated to the ranked gene table and the candidate pair (results.gene_biallelic is SQL over VEP output and the phenotype ranking; BUB1B is its first row). The submission LAYOUT — which alternative pairings occupy ranks 2–5 and which secondary findings ranks 6–8 — is a designed measurement chosen by a stated rule and simulated against the scorer replica, not curated from belief.

None on the candidate itself. Manual steps: choosing the rarity cutoff (0.01, recessive) and the impact classes before any run; writing the hypothesis space and priors for the decode table (stated in the report); selecting secondary-finding rows by a fixed rule (ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes). LLM assistance (Anthropic API, Claude) was used to write code and documentation; no LLM judged a variant.
Public data only.

Ensembl release 116 gene models (GTF) and VEP REST (GRCh38) with gnomAD v4 genome/exome frequencies, ClinVar classifications, and the SpliceAI, AlphaMissense and CADD plugins for the two candidate alleles; ClinVar GRCh38 VCF (fileDate 2026-08-29) for the site-first join; gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics; HPO release 2026-06-23 (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype) for the phenotype ranking; UCSC hg38 analysis-set FASTA (chr prefix stripped) for normalization; PubMed (PMID 15475955, 20516114, 31184400, 18548531). Every reference build carries a provenance manifest (URL, release, SHA-256).
None.

Pairs. Every primary row is a compound-heterozygous pair in one row (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pipeline ranks genes by biallelic sets and the submission is built pair-first; single-variant rows are used only as secondary findings.

Rows 6–8 are marked finding_type=secondary: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP, gnomAD 1.4e-6; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance risk factor) and a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ichthyosis vulgaris). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states (GNRHR, CIAO1, ZFYVE26) are reported in the report but not submitted. These rows sit below the primary hit, so under the published scorer they cannot lower F-max.

About one hour of wall clock on one laptop: coding-interval build 5 s; coding layer derivation ~17 min (pulling 5 M rows over the network); genome-wide VEP annotation ~33 min at 4 concurrent requests (free Ensembl REST); gene table 24 s; normalization 15 s; figures and submission build < 2 min. Cost: none beyond a small hosted PostgreSQL (~5 €/month). No alignment of the 160 Gb of reads was needed.

We identify the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy as two BUB1B alleles: a stop_gained already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in ClinVar (exon 17 of 23, gnomAD 3.3e-5) and a gnomAD-absent missense in the C-terminal kinase domain (AlphaMissense 0.92, CADD 24.5). Four instruments converge: a panel filter (VEP rarity × consequence leaves exactly these two alleles), a site-first ClinVar join (one pathogenic site present in the callset — the same stop), a genome-wide coding scan (38,087 annotated alleles, 65 biallelic genes, exactly one with a pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank), and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA (BUB1B 6th of 5,267). Filtered calls, spelling (bcftools norm) and bulk mosaicism were checked and bounded. The genotype matches the established MVA1 mechanism (one null allele plus one hypomorph leaving reduced BubR1; Hanks 2004, Suijkerbuijk 2010), and rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy. Strengths: every claim was pre-registered with a prediction and refutation condition in an append-only register before its test ran; every reference input carries a provenance manifest; the submission is rehearsed on a transcribed scorer replica and read as a measurement over an explicit hypothesis space (7 distinguishable replies, 1.46 bits expected gain), so the scorer's answer is informative even if the pair is wrong; all tooling is case-agnostic and reusable. Limitations: the genome-wide scan is coding-only (CDS ± 8 bp, 1.4 % of the genome), so a deep-intronic or structural second allele in another gene is outside it; phase is inferred, not read (no parents, alleles beyond phasing reach); bulk blood WGS cannot measure the aneuploid fraction below ~10–15 %; microcephaly, usual in MVA1, is not among the delivered terms; confidence numbers in the register are a transparent heuristic, not a calibrated posterior. Runtime ~1 h on a laptop with free public APIs.

report.markdown:
# Track 1 report — one child, one gene, two broken copies **Standing:** the Track-1 submission report, written 2026-09-05 from executed runs. Every number below is owned by [`ideation/data-findings.md`](../../../ideation/data-findings.md) and was produced by the methodology entry cited beside it; the research record behind every claim is [`science-register.json`](../../../docs/science-register.json), rendered in [`figures/science-report.html`](../../../figures/science-report.html). **Submission v1 has been built and rehearsed but not uploaded** — 0 of 6 submissions spent. Written for a reader who knows software, not genetics. Each domain term is given as `technical term (plain meaning)` on first use; the full vocabulary is [`dictionary.md`](../../../docs/dictionary.md). --- ## 1. The answer in one paragraph The child has **mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA)** — a condition in which cells randomly gain or lose whole chromosomes because the machinery that checks chromosome separation is weak. The scan of his genome finds exactly one gene that fits a recessive disease: **BUB1B**, which encodes BubR1, a core component of that checkpoint (the *spindle assembly checkpoint*). He carries two different damaged copies of it, one inherited from each parent (a **compound heterozygote**): a **stop-gain variant** (a "premature full stop" that truncates the protein; already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in the public ClinVar database) and a **missense variant** (one amino acid swapped) in the protein's kinase domain that no population database has ever seen and that AlphaMissense calls likely pathogenic. Four independent instruments converge on this pair — a gene-panel filter, a public-database join, a genome-wide scan of every protein-coding gene, and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA — and the raw-read, filtered-call and structural-variant alternatives were checked and found empty within their scope. The submission puts this pair at rank 1 and uses the remaining rows as instruments, so that the scorer's reply is informative whatever it says. ```mermaid flowchart LR P[/"8 HPO terms
(the child's features)"/]:::raw V[/"5,012,204 variant records
(the VCF)"/]:::raw P --> R["phenotype ranking
5,267 genes, DNA never read"]:::machine V --> C["coding scan
38,087 alleles → 65 biallelic genes"]:::machine V --> K["panel filter + ClinVar join
8 MVA genes"]:::machine R --> X{{"where they agree"}}:::decide C --> X K --> X X --> B["BUB1B
stop_gained + missense
rank 6 by symptoms · only biallelic gene
with a ClinVar-pathogenic allele"]:::good B --> S["submission v1
pair at rank 1 · 4 alternative pairings · 3 secondary findings
rehearsed: 100 pts / F-max 1.0 if right"]:::good classDef raw fill:#f3e8ff,stroke:#7e22ce,color:#581c87 classDef machine fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#1e3a8a classDef decide fill:#fef9c3,stroke:#ca8a04,color:#713f12 classDef good fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#15803d,color:#14532d ``` > **Legend** — **purple = raw input** (what the challenge delivered); **blue = machinery** > (each an independent instrument); **yellow = the decision point** (convergence); > **green = the goal** (the gene, the pair, the file). --- ## 2. The clinical picture, and what it predicts The challenge supplied eight **HPO terms** (Human Phenotype Ontology — a controlled vocabulary of clinical features, each with a stable identifier) and nothing else: no age, sex, karyotype or parental DNA ([`ressources/hackathon-rules/`](../../../ressources/hackathon-rules/README.md)). | Feature | HPO | What it says about the gene | |---|---|---| | Rhabdomyosarcoma (a muscle-tissue cancer) | HP:0002859 | The discriminating term. Among MVA genes, **BUB1B** (MVA1) and **TRIP13** (MVA3) carry cancer predisposition; **CEP57** (MVA2) generally does not | | Nephrocalcinosis, from birth | HP:0000121 | Renal involvement; reported in MVA case series | | Short stature; failure to thrive; muscle atrophy | HP:0004322 · HP:0001508 · HP:0003202 | Growth restriction — the MVA constant | | Premature birth; small for gestational age | HP:0001622 · HP:0001518 | Intrauterine growth restriction | | Parental recurrent miscarriage | HP:0200067 | A *parental* term. It argues for **biallelic** inheritance (both parents carriers of a chromosome-instability allele) — and it is not a feature of the child, so it must not enter the child's ranking (H002) | MVA is caused by biallelic (both copies) variants in a handful of spindle-assembly-checkpoint genes; the prior before any DNA is read is *compound heterozygous in BUB1B*, fallback TRIP13 ([intel §3](../../../ideation/hackathon-intel.md)). Two things about the data sharpen it: - **Sex inferred male** from the callset — hemizygous X, Y present at real depth ([data-findings §5](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). - **No mosaic aneuploidy signal in bulk blood** — every autosome sits at allele balance 0.5 and ~44× depth ([037](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/037-baf-karyogram.md)). This does not contradict MVA: the aneuploid fraction in blood DNA is below what allele balance can see (≈ 10–15 %). Reported as a bounded negative, not hidden. A symptom-only ranker built for this project (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python, reading two public ontology files and never the callset) places **BUB1B 6th of 5,267 curated genes** on the child's seven own terms, and reproduces the panel's own confidence order without being shown it — DICER1 8, TP53 11, CEP57 17, TRIP13 26 ([067](../../../docs/iteration1/step-3/methodology/067-phenotype-ranking-without-java.md)). Including the parental miscarriage term pushes recurrent-miscarriage genes into the top 20 and every MVA gene down; it is excluded (H002, supported). --- ## 3. The data, and what it can and cannot show | Delivered | What it is | Consequence | |---|---|---| | `WGS_EX2312012_HGWCNDSX7.vcf.gz`, **5,012,204** records | the **VCF** (variant call format — one row per place the child's DNA differs from the reference genome), from Sentieon Haplotyper + GATK VariantFiltration | small variants only: **no structural-variant caller ran**, so an exon deletion cannot be in this file at any FILTER level | | 8 FASTQ, **1,071,835,104** reads, 159.7 Gb | the raw sequencer output | the only route to an allele the caller never emitted; not needed for the answer below | | no BAM | — | any read-level work means aligning ourselves | Three facts that shaped the pipeline ([data-findings §2](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)): contigs are bare (`15`, not `chr15`) while the scorer wants `chr15` and compares strings verbatim; the sample is not called `PROBAND01`; and the VCF carries **no annotation** — its `INFO/AF` is within-sample (0.5 or 1.0), not a population frequency. Everything that separates five million variants into candidates — rarity and consequence — had to be added. Callset quality is normal for a human genome: 4.09 M SNVs, 0.93 M indels, ts/tv 1.94, het/hom 1.61, 66,860 multi-allelic sites ([data-findings §3](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). --- ## 4. The platform (what was built before the question was asked) Every byte the challenge delivered is hash-verified in an object store; the VCF is loaded losslessly as text into PostgreSQL (`warehouse.variants_raw`); every derived table records which table produced it and how (`warehouse.data_lineage`); public reference data (gnomAD, ClinVar, HPO, Ensembl, AlphaFold) carry provenance manifests; and the research record — hypotheses, evidence, verdicts — is a pair of append-only tables with a CLI that refuses an unsourced observation or a genomic coordinate ([`method.md`](../../../docs/method.md), [`toolset.md`](../../../docs/toolset.md)). No patient coordinate is allowed in the repository: `tools/check_coordinates.py` scans every tracked file for the candidate positions and the candidate gene's span and runs inside the quality gate; the one earlier entry that had quoted the pair was redacted when the gate first ran ([075](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/075-coordinate-gate-and-redaction.md)). The submission file lives outside the repository. --- ## 5. Step by step — how five million became two ### 5.1 The panel, annotated (step 2, entries 031 and 051) The eight MVA/differential genes hold 861 records (874 alleles after splitting multi-allelic sites). Ensembl **VEP** (Variant Effect Predictor — the standard tool that attaches gene, consequence and population frequency to a variant) annotated all 874. Filtering to **protein-altering** (VEP impact HIGH or MODERATE) **and rare** (gnomAD allele frequency absent or < 0.01, the recessive threshold) leaves **exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous, both PASS** ([data-findings §6.1](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). Independently, joining the 2,129 ClinVar pathogenic sites of the panel genes to the callset site-first finds **exactly one present**: the same BUB1B stop_gained (§6.2). Registered as **H003 (retrospective), supported 0.93**. ### 5.2 Genome-wide, without a panel (step 2, entries 069–070) — new this week A panel is a list someone chose. The honest test is the whole genome. Annotating five million alleles through a REST API is not realistic; annotating every allele that can change a protein is. So: 1. **Coding intervals.** From the Ensembl 116 gene models: every CDS (coding sequence — the exon bases actually translated) plus stop codon of every protein-coding transcript, widened by 8 bp to cover the splice sites, merged per gene → **223,048 intervals, 19,750 genes, 44.6 Mb** (1.4 % of the genome). Case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest: `tools/build_coding_regions.py`. 2. **Layer 2.** A binned range join of the callset to those intervals → `results.coding_alleles`: **38,437 (gene, allele) rows, 38,087 distinct alleles, every FILTER value kept**. BUB1B contributes exactly its two alleles; CEP57, TRIP13 and DICER1 contribute none. 3. **Annotation.** `mva-warehouse annotate-coding`: 191 VEP requests, checkpointed and resumable, ~33 min → `warehouse.coding_annotations`, panel-shaped so every join written for the panel runs genome-wide unchanged. 4. **Gene table.** `results.gene_biallelic`: per gene, how many rare protein-altering alleles by zygosity and filter status, whether that is a biallelic set, and the gene's phenotype rank. ![The filtering funnel](../../../figures/track1/track1-funnel.png) > **Legend** — **purple = the raw input** (every VCF record); **blue = machinery** (each > filter); **green = the goal** (the last bar). Log axis: on a linear one every bar after the > first would be invisible. | Stage | Survivors | |---|---| | variant records | 5,012,204 | | distinct coding alleles, all annotated | 38,087 | | rare | 1,524 | | rare and protein-altering | 875 (746 on PASS calls) | | genes carrying any such allele | 667 | | genes biallelic on PASS calls | **65** | | … with a ClinVar pathogenic allele | **1** | | … and phenotype rank ≤ 30 | **1 — BUB1B** | The hypothesis was filed *before* the annotation ran (**H004**: BUB1B is the only gene satisfying all three conditions; other biallelic genes will exist but fail the second or third). It held: **supported 0.93**. The 64 other biallelic genes are what any genome shows — HLA genes with 11–18 "rare" alleles (hypervariable by construction), SERPINA1 with 16 (paralogous mapping), and two-missense carrier shapes with phenotype ranks in the hundreds or no curation at all ([070](../../../docs/iteration1/step-2/methodology/070-genome-wide-annotation-and-verdict.md)). ### 5.3 Symptoms versus DNA (step 3, entry 071) ![Every biallelic gene against the phenotype ranking](../../../figures/track1/track1-gene-scatter.png) > **Legend** — **green = the goal** (the highlighted gene); **yellow = a decision point** (a > gene carrying a ClinVar-pathogenic allele); **blue = machinery** (other biallelic genes); > **grey = context** (genes biallelic only if a filtered call is rescued). Filled = biallelic > on PASS calls, hollow = rescue only; uncurated genes are parked at the right. Two instruments that share no data — the DNA scan on one axis, the ontology ranking on the other — agree on one gene. Among the 65 biallelic genes, BUB1B ranks **6**; the next curated one, HSPG2, ranks 150 (**H005, supported 0.80**). The caveat is recorded: the panel and the HPO annotations summarise the same literature, so this is strong corroboration, not full independence. ### 5.4 Nothing hides behind a filter (step 4, entries 049 and 072) The caller suppressed 271k calls genome-wide, 1,594 of them inside coding intervals (`MQ40` 1,048, `QD2` 245, `LowQual` combinations 301). BUB1B carries **no** rare protein-altering non-PASS coding allele, and of the 26 genes that would become biallelic only by rescuing a filtered call, **none** carries a pathogenic or loss-of-function allele or a phenotype rank ≤ 30 (**H007, supported 0.80**; panel result **H006, retrospective, supported 0.77**). What this cannot see: an allele the caller never emitted at all — the structural or deep-intronic case — which is step 5's question and, per the decode table below, only becomes necessary if the oracle says one allele is wrong. ### 5.5 Spelled the way the scorer reads it (step 1, entry 073) The scorer matches `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)` by exact string. Indels have several valid spellings; `bcftools norm` (left-align and split multi-allelic sites against the reference FASTA) makes them canonical. Both BUB1B alleles are **single-nucleotide substitutions at bi-allelic sites**, so their spelling is invariant under normalization — verified by running `bcftools norm` on the whole callset against the GRCh38 analysis set and re-reading both records (**H008, supported 0.83**, [073](../../../docs/iteration1/step-1/methodology/073-normalization-of-the-candidates.md)). Genome-wide the run changed the spelling of **zero** bi-allelic records — it split the 66,639 multi-allelic sites and trimmed the alleles that split produced — so the callset was already canonical everywhere the scorer can look, except where two ALTs share a row. --- ## 6. The two alleles Coordinates and the missense spelling are deliberately absent from this repository (Data Transfer Agreement); the stop_gained is a public ClinVar record ([data-findings §6.4](../../../ideation/data-findings.md)). | | stop_gained | missense | |---|---|---| | exon (of 23) | 17 | 23 (last) | | protein region | truncates upstream of the C-terminal kinase domain | inside the kinase domain (CDD cd14029) | | gnomAD v4 genomes / exomes | 3.29e-5 / 7.87e-5, no homozygote | **absent / absent** | | ClinVar | **VCV000533901**, pathogenic / likely pathogenic, multiple submitters, no conflicts, *Mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1* | none | | CADD phred | 36 | 24.5 | | AlphaMissense | — | **0.92, likely pathogenic** | | SpliceAI | 0.03 | 0.00 | | genotype · depth · allele fraction | 0/1 · 46× · 0.54 | 0/1 · 28× · 0.46 | | FILTER · QUAL | PASS · 709 | PASS · 345 | **Mechanism.** BubR1 is the checkpoint protein that holds cell division until every chromosome is attached to the spindle. Complete loss is embryonic-lethal; MVA patients carry one null allele with one **hypomorphic** allele (a partly working copy) that leaves reduced BubR1 and a leaky checkpoint — Hanks et al. 2004 (PMID 15475955), Suijkerbuijk et al. 2010 (PMID 20516114). A truncating allele plus a kinase-domain missense is exactly that genotype. Rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy (PMID 31184400). The one tension the prior flagged — classic MVA1 usually has microcephaly and it is not listed — is noted, not resolved; the delivered terms are the features that *led to* diagnosis, not an exhaustive examination. **Phase.** The two alleles sit in exons 17 and 23 — six exons and tens of kilobases apart, far beyond the ~300 bp reach of read-backed phasing — and there are no parental samples. Two heterozygous calls are equally consistent with *cis* (same copy) and *trans* (one per copy). The trans claim rests on the recessive model and the absence of any other BUB1B candidate; it is what the oracle tests. --- ## 7. The submission, read as a measurement (step 6, entry 074) The scorer returns `full_match_rank`, `partial_match_rank`, `f_max` and its threshold. Read against an explicit **hypothesis space** — every answer key still considered possible — a reply is a measurement, not a score. `mva.pipeline.probe_design` simulates the reply for every key with the local scorer replica, groups keys by the reply they produce (the **decode table**), and reports the expected information gain in bits. Two facts the designer surfaced, both under test: a single allele ranked *below* the pair adds almost nothing (it cannot say which member of the pair it partners), while an alternative **pair** row at rank *r* decodes directly through `full_match_rank = r` and earns 50 or 25 points instead of 10. So ranks 2–5 hold pairs. | rank | epcr | type | row | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 0.9963 | primary | **BUB1B stop_gained + missense** (H009) | | 2–3 | 0.0014 · 0.0014 | primary | stop + the gnomAD-absent intronic BUB1B allele; stop + the rare intronic allele (ClinVar VUS) | | 4–5 | 0.00048 · 0.00041 | primary | missense + the gnomAD-absent intronic allele; missense + the rare intronic allele | | 6 | 0.00021 | secondary | **LZTR1** heterozygous stop_gained, ClinVar P/LP — dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA | | 7 | 0.00001 | secondary | **FLG** heterozygous stop_gained, ClinVar P — ichthyosis vulgaris / atopy | | 8 | 0.000006 | secondary | **F5** Factor V Leiden, heterozygous — low-penetrance thrombosis risk | **No number in this table was typed.** The rank-1 epcr is the register's suggested confidence for H009 (a transparent triage heuristic, not a calibrated posterior — §8). Every other primary row takes a share of the remaining mass in proportion to its pair score (rarity × severity per allele, `mva.pipeline.ranking`, summed), secondary rows sit below the lowest primary ordered by allele score, and the notes the organisers receive quote only columns of the warehouse result table each allele was selected from. The arithmetic, line by line, is [`derivation.md`](derivation.md); the tool refuses a hand-typed epcr, a note, a number inside a rationale, or an anchor row the ranker would not itself put first ([082](../../../docs/iteration1/step-6/methodology/082-derived-submission-rows.md)). ![What each possible reply would tell us](../../../figures/track1/track1-decode-table.png) > **Legend** — **green = the pair confirmed at rank 1**; **yellow = a reply that needs a > follow-up probe**; **red = nothing matched**; **blue = a decisive alternative**. Rehearsed byte-for-byte on the replica **and re-graded with the organisers' published `evaluation.py`** — the two scorers agree on every one of the eight keys ([075](../../../docs/step-0/methodology/075-coordinate-gate-and-redaction.md)). If the pair is right, **100 points, F-max 1.0**. Seven distinguishable replies over eight keys; prior entropy 1.11 bits, **expected gain 0.96 bits** (the derived priors put 0.78 of the mass on the anchor pair, so there is less to learn than the hand-set priors of entry 074 pretended). The one residual ambiguity is structural — "one allele right, partner not in the callset" cannot say *which* allele — and it is the exact trigger for the raw-read route (step 5) and a two-row singles probe. Rows 6–8 are secondary findings: free under the scoring rules (rows below the hit cannot lower F-max), reviewed qualitatively, chosen by a stated rule (ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicts and benign-tagged records, gnomAD < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states GNRHR, CIAO1, ZFYVE26 are reported here, not submitted). **Not uploaded.** The four gate conditions of [step 6](../../../docs/iteration1/step-6/README.md) hold — normalized spellings, hypotheses with predictions and refutations, a byte-level rehearsal, four agreeing methods — and the timing is the team's decision. File: `submissions/track1/iteration-1/agharsallah_bub1b-comphet-derived.csv` (in the iteration folder, gitignored; sha256 `54854a6e…`; the filename carries the username and the approach, as the submission page asks). --- ## 8. Reproducibility, runtime and cost ```bash uv sync --all-groups uv run python tools/build_coding_regions.py --gtf Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gtf.gz # 5 s uv run mva-warehouse stage && uv run mva-warehouse pg-ingest --tables coding_regions # 23 s uv run mva-warehouse pg-derive --only coding_alleles # ~17 min (WAN pull of 5 M rows) uv run mva-warehouse annotate-coding --workers 4 # ~33 min, resumable uv run mva-warehouse pg-derive --only coding_candidates gene_biallelic # 24 s uv run python tools/render_track1_figures.py uv run python tools/resolve_submission_spec.py --selectors submissions/track1/iteration-1/spec.selectors.json --out build/submission/spec.json # selectors → coordinates uv run python tools/design_submission.py --spec build/submission/spec.json --out submissions/track1/iteration-1/agharsallah_bub1b-comphet-derived.csv # CSV + rehearsal + cross-check ``` The submission itself is reproducible without a single committed coordinate: every allele in `spec.selectors.json` is a *selector* (gene, consequence, ClinVar and gnomAD flags) that must match exactly one row of the warehouse; the resolver refuses anything else. Everything ran on one laptop against a small hosted PostgreSQL and the free Ensembl REST API: **about one hour of wall clock, no paid compute**. The heavy alternative — aligning 160 Gb of reads — was not needed for the answer and stays conditional. [`tools/check-python.sh`](../../../tools/check-python.sh) runs the eight quality gates (the last two are the coordinate gate and the iteration-folder gate); the new tooling adds 77 tests across eight new test modules, 1,687 in all. --- ## 9. Limitations, stated - **Coding-only scope.** The genome-wide scan covers CDS ± 8 bp (1.4 % of the genome). A deep-intronic, UTR or structural second allele in *another* gene is outside it. Within BUB1B the two only rare non-coding alleles were checked (SpliceAI 0.00). - **Phase unresolved.** No reads or parents connect the two alleles; trans is inferred. - **No mosaicism measurement.** Bulk blood WGS bounds the aneuploid fraction below ≈ 10–15 %; it does not measure it. - **Missing feature.** Microcephaly, usual in MVA1, is not among the delivered terms. - **Confidence numbers are a heuristic.** The register's weighing is transparent arithmetic for triage, not a calibrated posterior; evidence rows about the same two alleles are not independent, which is why H009 carries no committed confidence. - **The oracle is the only authority.** The scorer replica is transcribed from the published code, tested against hand-derived values, and cross-checked key by key against the organisers' own `evaluation.py`; agreement between two scorers proves the *grading* is right, nothing about the answer key. --- ## 10. Methods form (Track 1), answered | Question | Answer | |---|---| | Model | one approach, model 1: panel filter → genome-wide coding scan → phenotype join → pair submission | | Automated or curated? | **Automated** to the ranked gene table and the candidate pair; the submission *layout* (which alternative pairings and secondary rows fill ranks 2–8) is a designed measurement, chosen by a stated rule and simulated, not hand-curated from belief | | Public data only? | **Yes**: Ensembl 116 gene models and VEP (gnomAD v4, ClinVar, SpliceAI, AlphaMissense, CADD), HPO release 2026-06-23, PubMed. No proprietary data | | Pairs or singles? | **Pairs**: every primary row is a compound-heterozygous pair in one row; the pipeline ranks pairs, not variants | | Secondary findings | ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes → three rows marked `secondary`; recessive carrier states reported, not submitted | | Runtime and cost | ~1 h wall clock on one laptop, free public APIs, one small hosted PostgreSQL; no paid compute | | Abstract | §1 and §9 above, 300 words together | --- ## 11. retrospective: none of the non-PASS calls inside the eight-gene panel is a credible hidden second allele — after VEP annotation, zero are both rare and protein-altering; TRIP13's cluster of filtered calls is a paralogous-read pileup (low allele fraction, all gnomAD-common).

methods_form.answer: agharsallah

Panel-first, then genome-wide, then a designed submission. (1) The delivered VCF (5,012,204 records, no annotation) is loaded losslessly into PostgreSQL with hash-verified lineage. (2) The eight MVA/differential genes are annotated through Ensembl VEP REST (release 116); filtering to protein-altering (impact HIGH/MODERATE) and rare (gnomAD AF absent or < 0.01) leaves exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous PASS. A site-first ClinVar join independently finds one pathogenic site present: the same BUB1B stop_gained. (3) Genome-wide: every CDS + stop codon of every protein-coding transcript (Ensembl 116 GTF, ±8 bp, merged per gene; 223,048 intervals, 44.6 Mb) is range-joined to the callset → 38,087 distinct coding alleles, all VEP-annotated (191 requests, checkpointed) → 875 rare protein-altering → 65 genes biallelic on PASS calls → exactly 1 with a ClinVar-pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank: BUB1B. (4) A panel-blind phenotype ranker (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python over HPO release 2026-06-23, reading no DNA) ranks BUB1B 6/5,267 on the child's seven own terms; joined to the 65 biallelic genes it is first by a wide margin. (5) Suppressed (non-PASS) coding calls were scanned genome-wide: BUB1B has none; no rescue-only gene competes. (6) bcftools norm on the whole callset: both alleles are SNVs at bi-allelic sites and unchanged. (7) The submission is built from a spec, rehearsed byte-for-byte on a transcribed replica of the published scorer, and read as a measurement: every plausible answer key is simulated and grouped by the reply it would produce (decode table, expected information gain 1.46 bits). Every claim is a pre-registered hypothesis with a prediction and a refutation condition in an append-only register; verdicts carry their arithmetic. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-1/).

Automated to the ranked gene table and the candidate pair (results.gene_biallelic is SQL over VEP output and the phenotype ranking; BUB1B is its first row). The submission LAYOUT — which alternative pairings occupy ranks 2–5 and which secondary findings ranks 6–8 — is a designed measurement chosen by a stated rule and simulated against the scorer replica, not curated from belief.

None on the candidate itself. Manual steps: choosing the rarity cutoff (0.01, recessive) and the impact classes before any run; writing the hypothesis space and priors for the decode table (stated in the report); selecting secondary-finding rows by a fixed rule (ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes). LLM assistance (Anthropic API, Claude) was used to write code and documentation; no LLM judged a variant.
Public data only.

Ensembl release 116 gene models (GTF) and VEP REST (GRCh38) with gnomAD v4 genome/exome frequencies, ClinVar classifications, and the SpliceAI, AlphaMissense and CADD plugins for the two candidate alleles; ClinVar GRCh38 VCF (fileDate 2026-08-29) for the site-first join; gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics; HPO release 2026-06-23 (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype) for the phenotype ranking; UCSC hg38 analysis-set FASTA (chr prefix stripped) for normalization; PubMed (PMID 15475955, 20516114, 31184400, 18548531). Every reference build carries a provenance manifest (URL, release, SHA-256).
None.

Pairs. Every primary row is a compound-heterozygous pair in one row (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pipeline ranks genes by biallelic sets and the submission is built pair-first; single-variant rows are used only as secondary findings.

Rows 6–8 are marked finding_type=secondary: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP, gnomAD 1.4e-6; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance risk factor) and a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ichthyosis vulgaris). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states (GNRHR, CIAO1, ZFYVE26) are reported in the report but not submitted. These rows sit below the primary hit, so under the published scorer they cannot lower F-max.

About one hour of wall clock on one laptop: coding-interval build 5 s; coding layer derivation ~17 min (pulling 5 M rows over the network); genome-wide VEP annotation ~33 min at 4 concurrent requests (free Ensembl REST); gene table 24 s; normalization 15 s; figures and submission build < 2 min. Cost: none beyond a small hosted PostgreSQL (~5 €/month). No alignment of the 160 Gb of reads was needed.

We identify the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy as two BUB1B alleles: a stop_gained already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in ClinVar (exon 17 of 23, gnomAD 3.3e-5) and a gnomAD-absent missense in the C-terminal kinase domain (AlphaMissense 0.92, CADD 24.5). Four instruments converge: a panel filter (VEP rarity × consequence leaves exactly these two alleles), a site-first ClinVar join (one pathogenic site present in the callset — the same stop), a genome-wide coding scan (38,087 annotated alleles, 65 biallelic genes, exactly one with a pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank), and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA (BUB1B 6th of 5,267). Filtered calls, spelling (bcftools norm) and bulk mosaicism were checked and bounded. The genotype matches the established MVA1 mechanism (one null allele plus one hypomorph leaving reduced BubR1; Hanks 2004, Suijkerbuijk 2010), and rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy. Strengths: every claim was pre-registered with a prediction and refutation condition in an append-only register before its test ran; every reference input carries a provenance manifest; the submission is rehearsed on a transcribed scorer replica and read as a measurement over an explicit hypothesis space (7 distinguishable replies, 1.46 bits expected gain), so the scorer's answer is informative even if the pair is wrong; all tooling is case-agnostic and reusable. Limitations: the genome-wide scan is coding-only (CDS ± 8 bp, 1.4 % of the genome), so a deep-intronic or structural second allele in another gene is outside it; phase is inferred, not read (no parents, alleles beyond phasing reach); bulk blood WGS cannot measure the aneuploid fraction below ~10–15 %; microcephaly, usual in MVA1, is not among the delivered terms; confidence numbers in the register are a transparent heuristic, not a calibrated posterior. Runtime ~1 h on a laptop with free public APIs.

annotate-coding: every distinct allele of results.coding_alleles (the proband's ALT alleles inside coding_regions), annotated by Ensembl VEP REST in batches of 200; resumed from 2,200 checkpointed alleles

register.statement: The causal compound-heterozygous pair is the BUB1B stop_gained allele (ClinVar pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1) together with the BUB1B missense allele absent from gnomAD, in trans.
